SddMigrationV1V2.keywords: migration, v1, v2, upgrade, tasks-to-specs, task-id, slug, anchors, compression, decision-merge, restructure, plan-first, sdd-migration, comprehension-pass, inventory-reverse
SddMigrationV1V2.Mission:
Migrate a repo from the SDD v1 layout to v2 — interactively, plan-first, under git (baseline first — every step is revertible). Entered when `sdd-state` reports `FLOW_VERSION=v1` (a `tasks/` directory), from the router preflight or any door. This is a SPECIFIC v1→v2 directive; a later `v2→v3` is its own sibling. Self-sufficient: it may run without the router core, so it repeats the operator-facing axioms it needs.
Not a mechanical copy. Changing decisions changes their references in code, so the migration reads and touches code, and it compresses: decisions and discussion threads that converged on the same thing during the document's evolution are collapsed (the compression protocol is loaded lazily). The operator first sees the whole plan — current → target, how many passes, what moves where, which IDs change, which decisions merge, which files are touched, what gets optimized — and acknowledges it before anything is written.
Input — a v1 repo + the `sdd-migrate` / `sdd-state` / `sdd-check` tools. Output — a v2 repo (co-located `specs/`, slug Task-IDs, anchored tickets, compressed decisions, flat-Russian prose) that passes `sdd-state` v2 + `sdd-check` clean. Out of scope: authoring new specs (the scope/module branches) — migration only transforms what already exists.

BeliefState.Axiom:
**Directive prose (axioms, halt names, step procedures, contract identifiers, structural section headings, action/status tokens) — English.**
**Operator-facing artifact prose and operator-facing messages — Russian.** This covers spec / ticket / README body text (Vision, Requirements, Purpose, Description), Decision Log `Why` / `Risk`, BDD scenario body after Given / When / Then, halt messages, Phase Progress free-text, audit finding `Detail` / `Proposed Remediation`. Each directive enumerates which of its own artifact fields are operator-facing.
**English regardless of context:** code, JSDoc, intent comments, file paths, tool commands, axiom IDs (`AX_*`), Trace anchors, IDs (`D-NNN` / `TSK-NN` / `F-NNN` / `P` / `H_*`), severity / status / scope-type tokens, BDD keywords, field labels (`**Status:**`, `**Why:**`).

The SDD mechanical tools are `gennady` CLI commands. When working IN the gennady repo itself (including any of its worktrees), invoke them repo-relative from the working tree's own root — `npx tsx /cli/gennady.ts ` — never a hardcoded path to a different checkout; this is rewritten to `npx gennady ` by the path-normalizer when the directives are synced into a project. In every OTHER project, invoke the published package: `npx gennady `. Tools: `sdd-state`, `sdd-task`, `sdd-extract`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-log`, `sdd-sync`, `sdd-check`, `sdd-new`, `sdd-migrate`, `orient`, `lint`, `yagni`, `testcov`. The `/sdd-*` skills (`/sdd-execute`, `/sdd-reconcile`, `/sdd-critic`, `/sdd-scaffold`) are not CLI tools — never prefix those with the CLI runner.

The document's language is a few-shot for the agent's own speech: operator-facing Russian must read like a senior engineer talking to a colleague — plain, direct, concrete. Sounding smart or sharp is the failure mode, not the goal. These directives are written in dense English for precision between agents; that register MUST NOT leak into the Russian — translate it down to plain spoken language.
Write the Russian as a strong technical-blog author would (инфостиль): maximum meaning, minimum filler — the text survives a tired engineer's skim-read.
Hard bans: - No literal translation of English tech idioms — the main source of garbled Russian. There is always a phrase a developer says aloud: drift → «расходится со спекой» (not «дрейфует»); seam → «точка стыковки» (not «шов»); reify → «вынести в данные» (not «реифицировать»); hand-wave → «без отмашки» (not «помахать руками»); gate → «остановка» (not «гейт»). - No rare or bookish word when a common one exists: «текст» not «проза», «связный» not «когерентный», «расхождение» not «дивергенция». - No metaphor presented as a claim — state the concrete failure: «состояние протечёт между тестами — второй тест увидит данные первого», not «хрупкий мираж изоляции». - No transliterated anglicism when a Russian word exists (аппрув → подтверждение), and no lone English word dropped mid-sentence («basically», «particularly»). - No ornamental adjectives, no aphorisms. - Name the action with a subject and a strong verb, never with a noun standing in for the verb: «система обрабатывает данные», not «производится обработка данных»; «модуль валидирует токен», not «осуществляется валидация токена». Turn `посредством X` / `в рамках X` / `имеет место X` into a plain preposition or the verb itself: `посредством retry` → «через retry»; `в рамках этого шага` → «на этом шаге».
Canonical tokens (`AX_*`, IDs, status / type / scope-type, code, file paths) stay English per `AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`, shown as a tag beside the plain sentence — never as the sentence itself.
Test before sending: read it as a busy mid-level developer. Stumbled on a word, or it sounds like a blog showing off? Rewrite plainer. Would you say it aloud to a colleague at the next desk?
- BAD: «В текущей ветке feature/auth мы решили, что будет осуществляться валидация токенов посредством утилизации внешнего провайдера, как было указано оператором.» - GOOD: «Модуль валидирует токены через внешнего провайдера.» - Fixes: drops the session leak («текущая ветка feature/auth», «как было указано оператором» — per `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT`); replaces the bureaucratic noun-verb («осуществляется валидация») with subject+strong verb; drops the calque («утилизация» for «использование»).

The restructure step doubles as the comprehension pass — text turned into flat Russian that is still a cipher has not been fixed. Shares its vocabulary with `AX_LANGUAGE_QUALITY_CHECK` (`ai/directives/sdd-v2/audit.directive.xml`): empty label, metaphor-as-fact, code-only term. Here the agent APPLIES the fix while restructuring; audit only VERIFIES it later on a finished spec — do not defer this to a later pass.
For every sentence the restructure touches: - **Empty label** (adjective+noun with no stated opposite) → read the code the term describes and name the actual thing. `«тонкий тикет»` (thin relative to what?) → `«тикет без секции Phases Overview — только Meta и Decision Log»` (the exact shape the code check flags). - **Metaphor stated as fact** → the literal mechanism. `«спека и код разошлись»` → `«в Entity Inventory спеки объявлен экспорт, которого нет в коде — lint --inventory-reverse не находит его»`. - **Term whose meaning lives only in code** → decode it from the code, never guess. `«тяжёлая секция»` → `«секция длиннее 120 строк — порог SECTION_LINE_HARD_LIMIT_V2»` (read the constant, do not paraphrase the adjective). `«слаг»` on first use → `«человекочитаемый ID -, заменяющий числовой TSK-NN»`. - Cannot decode a term with confidence → ask the operator inline; a judgment call is not a tool-verifiable blocker, so it has no `H_*` — never guess, never silently drop the term. - Flatten the register per `AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE` in the same pass, not a second trip.

Move forward unless stopped — gated by confidence and stakes: - HIGH confidence + low-stakes step → show the result and proceed; the operator can object at any moment. - LOW confidence, OR a high-stakes step (architecture, pivot, a trust boundary, an irreversible choice) → hard stop, wait for the operator.
The agent never closes a step it is unsure about, and never auto-agrees to a risky shortcut (see `AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`).
Named hard stops — Approval Checks and the SCALE confirmation exchange — are exempt from the proceed rule; they always stop, however high the confidence.
Keep the dialogue compact: no repeat questions; group obvious questions into one; on long dialogues show the delta, not a full restate. Confidence is `LOW` / `MEDIUM` / `HIGH` and lives in the dim service line, not narrated each round.

The agent's job is to protect the operator from their own blind spots and lead them to a sound decision — even a junior operator. - Warn, don't only ask: name the risk that will hurt later, the requirement likely missing, the thing probably forgotten, the trust boundary (auth, payments, persistence) that needs a real runtime. - Pull the thread, don't fill a quota: after each answer, check whether it opened a new gap or risk; if so, follow it until the gap is actually closed — not until a question count is hit. - Ask developing questions — ones that deepen the topic and check what should and should NOT exist — not merely uncomfortable ones. Never announce a question; just ask it plainly. - Neutral and critical: if the operator wants to skip something risky, surface the cost and ask for a reason; never silently agree.
Blind-spot instincts (not a checklist to recite): canonical source of truth? behavior on dependency failure? where simulation ends and real runtime begins? who validates input here? which assumption, if wrong, kills the design?

Every fix must be operator-approved before execution. The plan is shown as a table. No edits are made before explicit operator "yes" / "go" / "ok". Operator may edit the plan (remove items, change classification, add notes).

The operator never sees the agent's machinery. No «DIRECTIVE ACTIVATED», no mode-detection narration, no «grounding collected», no «перехожу к STEP_2», no frame-stack talk. Detection, reading, and step transitions happen silently. Mode / scope / confidence live in the dim service line and the log, nowhere else.

Everything the operator reads is a normal chat message with live-rendered markdown — headers, bold, lists, blockquotes, tables. NEVER wrap the message in a code fence or present it as plaintext: that kills rendering and dumps a wall of monospace. Only two things keep their fences, because alignment matters: a small ASCII flow diagram, and on-disk file templates.

In `pivot` mode every replaced decision: the old D-NNN → `status: superseded`. The new D-NNN carries `Was → Now` + `Supersedes: D-NNN` + a git ref pointing to the pre-rework state. Pivot Invalidation List enumerates downstream artifacts requiring `refine-module` / reopen — consumed by `audit` via `AX_STALE_AFTER_PIVOT_VERIFICATION`.
`rewrite` mode is the exception: a pre-production / v0 scope with no production backing, whose old content was scratch that helps nothing going forward. It replaces the spec from a clean slate — NO supersession trail, NO Pivot Invalidation List (nothing downstream to keep coherent; git history is the only record). Use `pivot` (keep the trail) whenever the scope has any production backing or downstream consumers; use `rewrite` only for genuine v0 throwaway. Enforcement: a scope that already has downstream artifacts on disk (module specs or task tickets) is by definition NOT v0 — `rewrite` is forbidden there; halt and use `pivot`.

Separate Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses in every intake-style frame. - **Facts** — directly observable from input artifacts (spec, sibling specs, rule files, extracted measurements). - **Assumptions** — working assumptions awaiting confirmation; mark explicitly. - **Hypotheses** — conjectures that require operator validation before they are promoted to requirements.
Conflating the three causes downstream decisions to be made on unvalidated assumptions, producing requirements mismatches that surface only at integration; surface them in distinct lists.

KernelGrammar.Definition:
`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE(src)` tells the agent to READ the file at `src` and apply it as part of the current task. It is a runtime lazy-load, not text to inline into any output.
- The loaded branch directive INHERITS this kernel's cross-cutting core (language, dialogue, stateless) and carries only its own deltas; it MUST NOT repeat the core. - Loading is lazy: a branch is read only when its route fires, so the kernel stays small and context is not polluted by branches that do not apply. - The reference is a file path on purpose — a directive delivered as a file keeps full instruction priority, unlike command stdout.

ChatProtocol.Contract:
Questions must LOOK like questions and stay readable on any theme. A `### ❓ Вопросы — реши ` section header; each question numbered `Q`; options described in words. Never use `+` / `-` signs for pros / cons (they render black and vanish on dark themes). Group obvious sub-questions into one; do not pad the count.
Low-stakes — a recommendation is allowed, but only as the result of `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (not the first typical answer):
### ❓ Вопросы — реши «годится» = беру все рекомендации, или поправь по номерам.
**Q1 · <вопрос?>** ✅ **<рекомендованный вариант>** `[code]` — почему подходит именно под эту задачу. Иначе: - **<альтернатива>** `[code]` — _за: <плюс> · против: <минус>_
High-stakes / architecture — do NOT pre-anchor one pick. List the strongest candidates (include a non-obvious / tail one) with «за / против» and let the operator choose; or give a recommendation only alongside its strongest alternative and the reason it might win.
A plain binary question needs no list — recommendation + inline alternative:
**Q2 · <вопрос?>** ✅ **<рекомендация>** — почему. _или <короткая альтернатива>?_

A halt is a plain sentence first (what happened + what to do), with the token as a trailing tag:
🛑 <что случилось по-человечески> — <что сделать оператору> `[H_*]`

SddMigrationV1V2.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_OPERATOR_REJECTS_PLAN` | Operator declines the migration plan — stop; nothing is written | | `H_NOT_V1` | `sdd-state` does not report `FLOW_VERSION=v1` — there is nothing to migrate; return control | | `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL` | Final verification cannot reach v2 + clean and the gap is not recoverable in-flow — stop, report state, leave git baseline for rollback |

Step.Goal: Inventory the v1 repo deterministically — dry-runs only, no writes.
Step.Action: Confirm `FLOW_VERSION=v1` via `sdd-state` (else `H_NOT_V1`). Gather with tools, not by eye: `sdd-migrate plan --all .` (DRY-RUN — how many units, one per spec, and their ticket counts; orphan tickets surface here) and `sdd-migrate anchors --all .` (DRY-RUN — which tickets would be anchored / already are). Report the shape to the operator: units, tickets, orphans.

Step.Goal: Materialize the migration plan as an on-disk layer — the source of truth every later step consumes.
Step.Action: Run `sdd-migrate plan --all . --write`. This scaffolds `migration/` mirroring `specs/`: one `.migration.md` per spec — named from the spec's own filename with `.migration` inserted before the extension (`demo.spec.md` → `demo.spec.migration.md`) — carrying: a generated Inventory (facts a rescan can re-derive); a Section Map pre-filled by curated heading rules, `UNMAPPED` rows left for the agent; a Ticket Map pre-filled tolerantly from each ticket's v1 Meta (a New-ID guess when the v1 Meta already carries ACR/slug-shaped fields — a best-effort seed, not an authoritative fill, the agent still reviews and corrects it in STEP_3) with the Diagram Plan left fully to the agent; a per-unit step checklist — plus `migration/README.md` (the global G1–G8 order and the unit table). Explain to the operator, in plain Russian: the plan is files, not chat — it survives session breaks, it is verified mechanically (`plan --verify`), and its units are self-sufficient job cards that can be handed to parallel agents. Nothing outside `migration/` is written here.

Step.Goal: Make v1 tickets visible to the v2 tools.
Step.Action: Run `sdd-migrate anchors --all . --write` (deterministic — wraps canonical sections in `` markers; idempotent, skips already-anchored). Verify with `sdd-check` (anchor balance clean).

Step.Goal: Close the gaps the tool could not resolve — the Section Map arrives pre-filled; the agent reviews it and fills what a curated rule did not recognize.
Step.Action: `sdd-migrate plan --write` already ran `mapHeadingToSection` against every source heading and filled the **Section Map** for every heading a curated rule recognizes (action + target SECTION, e.g. `Module Vision` → `MODULE_VISION`); a heading no rule recognizes is left with target `UNMAPPED` — that row, and only that row, is this step's work. For each unit (parallelizable — a unit file is the worker's whole context): resolve every `UNMAPPED` row (keep / rename / merge / split / drop + the real target SECTION, from the scope-type's `*-spec-structure.xml`), spot-check the pre-filled rows against the source (a curated rule can be wrong on an atypical heading — fix it, do not defer to STEP_7), review and correct the **Ticket Map**'s tolerant v1-Meta pre-fill for every row (a row with no usable v1 Meta stays empty for the agent to fill from scratch): New ID `-` — `ACR` UPPERCASE, `slug` kebab-case from `Meta.Purpose`, unique repo-wide (`NEW_ID_REGEX` gates the grammar — the same slug twice means «one feature»; destination computed from the ID) — and the **Diagram Plan** (which diagram carries the mandatory Overview and from what content it is built; extra diagrams by judgment). Set the unit `**Status:** MAPPED`. Gate: `sdd-migrate plan --verify` — inventory unchanged, maps complete, zero `UNMAPPED` targets remaining, action vocabulary respected, slug grammar valid, zero cross-unit slug collisions. Fix and re-verify until clean.

Step.Goal: Operator sees the whole migration before anything outside `migration/` changes.
Step.Action: Present the verified layer, in plain Russian, facts separate from proposals (`AX_EVIDENCE_HYGIENE`): units and their section/ticket maps, the derived ID map, which decisions will merge (STEP_7), what gets simplified beyond a 1:1 copy, and the files+code the ID replacement will touch (from `sdd-migrate ids --from-plan` DRY-RUN counts). The operator confirms or edits (a scope to skip, a naming preference, a decision to keep) — `AX_OPERATOR_AGREEMENT`; `H_OPERATOR_REJECTS_PLAN` on decline. On go-ahead set units `**Status:** APPROVED`. STOP.

Step.Goal: Replace Task-IDs across specs, tickets, and code — mechanically.
Step.Action: Run `sdd-migrate ids --from-plan --write` (the map is derived from the approved Ticket Maps). The tool replaces exact IDs on word boundaries only — never a blind `TSK-[0-9]+` pattern, never non-IDs (`UTF-8`), never `D-NNN` / `FR-NN` / scope-prefixed requirement IDs — and gates itself on zero old IDs remaining. Then `sdd-check --all .` clean.

Step.Goal: Relocate tickets co-located and build the indexes — one scope at a time.
Step.Action: Per scope: `sdd-migrate move --scope --write` — relocates every ticket to its Ticket-Map destination (`git mv`, history kept): module co-location when the unit has a module (`specs///...`); a flat, scope-level destination is legal for a scope with no modules — the Ticket Map's destination decides, not a hardcoded module assumption. It rewrites every relative markdown link that pointed at a moved ticket (inside the moved tickets themselves and inside every other file in the same zones that referenced them by path). Backstop: `sdd-check` resolves ticket→spec references (`SDD_BROKEN_SPEC_REF` / `SDD_BROKEN_SPEC_ANCHOR`) and spec→spec links under `--all`, so a broken reference into a spec surfaces at the gate — but ticket→ticket links and arbitrary markdown links have no mechanical check yet: a link syntax the rewriter does not recognize, or a referencing file outside the zones, stays a manual follow-up. It also scaffolds `.3-tasks.md` + `.3-tasks.md` from ticket Meta (`MODULE_TASKS_INDEX_STRUCTURE` / `SCOPE_TASKS_INDEX_STRUCTURE`; the Cascade Table slot stays for the agent), and automatically removes the now-emptied `tasks//` — no separate cleanup step. Together (index present + tasks dir gone) that mechanically flips the scope to v2 — `sdd-check` detects flow per scope, so the migrated scope is now checked strictly while unmigrated neighbours stay lenient. A blocked move (unfilled map, stray ticket) stops that scope, not the run.

Step.Goal: Transform each spec to the v2 document structure — the per-unit semantic work.
Step.Action: For each unit (parallelizable — units do not share files; repo-wide mechanical steps are already done): execute the unit's S4–S6 checklist. Restructure the spec per its Section Map: target section order from the scope-type's `*-spec-structure.xml` (general → specific, arc42/C4), headings without numbers, heavy sections folded under ``, the Overview section carrying its diagram per the Diagram Plan. Restructuring reorders and clarifies what the source ALREADY says — per the Mission's out-of-scope line, migration only transforms what already exists: do not author a new section (Golden DX, FR, or any other) the source spec never had; a section the target structure calls for but the source lacks stays absent, marked for `evolve`/`sdd-continue` to fill later, never silently invented here. Collapse converged decisions via `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/compression.directive.xml")` (superseded marked per `AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION`, never silently dropped; merges propagated to code references) — a Decision Log entry's TEXT is changed only through supersession, never edited in place. Rewrite operator prose to flat engineering Russian in the same pass, per `AX_MIGRATION_COMPREHENSION_PASS` — decode every empty label and code-only term from the actual code, replace every metaphor with the literal mechanism, never guess (code / IDs / status tokens / BDD keywords / paths stay English). Gate per scope: `sdd-check --all specs/` — strict v2 structure, folds, real mermaid parse, and the language lint (`SDD_LANGUAGE_CALQUE`) that gates the comprehension pass above mechanically — clean. Set the unit `**Status:** DONE`.

Step.Goal: Prove the migration is complete; retire the working layer.
Step.Action: Final gate, all green or `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL`: `sdd-state` → `FLOW_VERSION=v2` · `sdd-check --all .` clean · zero original Task-IDs and zero `*.task-*.md` names remain (`sdd-migrate ids --from-plan` DRY-RUN reports nothing to do) · every unit `**Status:** DONE` · per migrated module, `gennady lint --spec= --inventory-reverse ` clean — the spec's Entity Inventory must match the code's real exports, not the migration's rewritten description of them. With the operator's confirmation remove the `migration/` layer (its content is now embodied in the repo; git history keeps the record). Return control to the caller — script readiness is the router's separate gate.

SddMigrationV1V2.ReferenceData:
**What changes:** `tasks///.task-NN.md` → co-located `specs///.task.-.md` + `*.3-tasks.md` indexes · `TSK-NN` (or `-NNN`) → `-` · tickets gain `` anchors · spec sections restructured to the v2 order (Overview + diagram, no heading numbers, heavy detail folded) · operator-prose → flat Russian · redundant decisions collapsed.
**What is NOT touched:** `D-NNN` (decision IDs, spec-local) stay · `FR-NN` / `NFC-NN` and scope-prefixed requirement/scenario IDs stay (optional later reformat to BDD `-REQ-N`) · `UTF-8` / `UTF-16` and similar are NOT IDs — never replaced.
**Tooling state — all four mechanical modes are real tools:** `sdd-migrate plan` (generate / `--verify` the migration layer — the Section Map arrives pre-filled by `mapHeadingToSection`; the Ticket Map's New-ID arrives pre-filled tolerantly from each ticket's v1 Meta where it already carries ACR/slug-shaped fields — a best-effort seed the agent still reviews, never authoritative; `--verify` fails on any leftover `UNMAPPED` target or a New ID that fails `NEW_ID_REGEX`, which requires `` UPPERCASE) · `sdd-migrate anchors` (section markers) · `sdd-migrate ids` (word-boundary ID replacement, `--from-plan`, self-gating on zero leftovers) · `sdd-migrate move` (per-scope relocation to the Ticket Map's destination — module co-location when the unit has a module, a flat scope-level destination legal for a scope without modules — + index scaffolding + relative markdown-link rewriting inside every moved ticket and every referencing file in the same zones + automatic removal of the now-emptied `tasks//`). What stays semantic — closing `UNMAPPED` rows and correcting the Ticket Map pre-fill (STEP_3) and the restructure/compression/comprehension pass (STEP_7) — is agent work executed against a verified plan and gated by strict per-scope `sdd-check` plus, at the final gate, `gennady lint --inventory-reverse` per migrated module (STEP_8).
**Mixed state is first-class:** `sdd-check` detects the flow version per scope. On a v1 repo a scope counts as migrated (v2, strict) only positively: `tasks//` removed AND the co-located `.3-tasks.md` present — both produced by `sdd-migrate move`. A scope that merely never had tasks stays lenient until the repo flips. Migration therefore runs one scope at a time — each migrated scope is checked strictly immediately, no waiting for the whole repo.
**Parallel dispatch:** unit files are self-sufficient — STEP_3 and STEP_7 fan out one unit per agent (units never share files); the repo-wide mechanical steps (anchors / ids / move) run centrally between the fan-outs, per `migration/README.md`'s G1–G8 order.
SddMigrationV1V2.ChatOutput:
Service line — dim, internal, never narrated (`AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`): `🔁 MIG_R · v1→v2 · step= · tickets= · ready=`.
A step-boundary / decision message (the decision card) is sectioned with markdown headers, in this order. Skip any section empty for this step. During free dialogue inside a step the agent does NOT print this layout — it just talks.
`` — internal anchor + scope + mode + confidence (supplied by the branch) `` — per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`
## `` `` — одной фразой, что делаем
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу — per `UNDERSTANDING_BLOCK_FORMAT` (goes at the TOP) ### главное решение — the crux in plain words; add a diagram per `FLOW_DIAGRAM_WHEN` if it is a flow ### ❓ Вопросы — реши N — per `QUESTION_FORMAT` ### ↓ Детали — по желанию — reasoning, full comparison, change-list (per `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE`)
One line under the service line: this session's milestones, each with a status marker — `✅` done · `▶️` now · `░` not yet. Delta only; never re-list everything already settled. This is the «where are we», and it replaces a verbose run-on of finished steps.
`<Веха>` ✅ · `<Веха>` ✅ · `<Веха>` ▶️ · `<Веха>` ░ · `<Веха>` ░
Decision first, reasoning on demand. The must-read top of a message is short: where we are + my read + what to decide. Everything heavy — full option comparison, evidence, the change-list, derivations — goes BELOW a `### ↓ Детали — по желанию` header. Never dump reasoning above the questions. Facts already verified collapse to one line («сверился: …»); uncertainties that need the operator BECOME the questions — never list them twice.
